mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP over two consecutive quarters indicates strong economic demand, which typically drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 50% of quarters with positive GDP growth, or GDP growth and SPX returns show a negative correlation over a 5-year period (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business confidence decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production by more than 1% over two consecutive months signals a contraction in supply, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are negatively impacted.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between INDPRO declines and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts by more than 5% over two consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as related industries benefit.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 jobs in a month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate and CPI both increase by more than 0.5% within a month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with monetary tightening, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns diminish.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL increases on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP and retail sales both show a decline of more than 1% over two consecutive quarters, it signals a weakening in economic demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are negatively impacted.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both decline > 1% over 2 quarters
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the joint effect of GDPC1 and RSAFS declines on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
